examples.en: Family discord leaves a big wound on a child.
He went through a hard time because of trouble at home.
The cause of the family discord was a lack of conversation.
They decided to move because of family discord.
I comforted a friend who is going through family troubles.
Family discord should be solved by talking to each other.

explain: 부부나 가족 사이의 다툼과 갈등을 말하는 조금 딱딱한 표현이에요. 뉴스나 상담, 글에서 많이 쓰고, 보통 대화에서는 '집안 문제', '집에 일이 있다'처럼 돌려 말해요. '가정불화를 겪다'가 자주 쓰는 짝이에요.
explain_en: It is a somewhat formal term for quarrels and conflict between spouses or family members. It appears in news, counseling and writing, while in casual talk people say things like '집안 문제'. '가정불화를 겪다' is a common collocation.

examples.ko: 부모님의 과잉보호 때문에 혼자 해 본 일이 별로 없어요.
examples.en: Because of my parents' overprotection, I've hardly done anything on my own.

examples.ko: 과잉보호는 아이가 스스로 크는 걸 방해할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Overprotection can get in the way of a child growing up on their own.

examples.ko: 저는 과잉보호 속에서 자라서 겁이 많아요.
examples.en: I grew up overprotected, so I'm easily scared.
I'm worried about whether overprotecting my child is good for them.

examples.ko: 엄마의 과잉보호가 조금 답답할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes my mom's overprotectiveness feels a bit suffocating.

examples.ko: 선생님은 과잉보호보다 믿고 기다려 주는 게 중요하다고 했어요.
examples.en: The teacher said trusting and waiting matters more than overprotecting.

explain: 주로 부모가 아이에게 '과잉보호를 하다', 아이가 '과잉보호를 받다'로 써요. '오냐오냐 키우다'는 뭐든 들어줘서 버릇없게 키운다는 느낌이라 조금 달라요.
explain_en: It mostly appears as '과잉보호를 하다' for parents and '과잉보호를 받다' for the child. '오냐오냐 키우다' means giving in to everything and spoiling a child, so it feels a bit different.

examples.en: I had a small quarrel with a friend.

examples.ko: 다툼 때문에 하루 종일 기분이 안 좋았어요.
examples.en: I was in a bad mood all day because of the quarrel.
We ended the quarrel and apologized to each other.
Even between a couple there are quarrels.
The police came because of the dispute with a neighbor.
Let us stop talking before it turns into a quarrel.

explain: '다투다'의 명사형이에요. 말이나 의견으로 맞설 때 어울리고, 몸으로 치고받는 일은 보통 '싸움'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the noun form of 'datuda'. It fits a clash of words or opinions; a physical fight is usually called 'ssaum'.

examples.ko: 화가 나도 사람에게 막말하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Even when you are angry, you should not say harsh things to people.
That person speaks rudely to anyone.
I regret saying harsh things to my brother yesterday.
I apologized right after saying those harsh things.
Many people throw rude remarks at each other in the comments.
I spoke rudely to my parents and got scolded badly.

explain: 화가 나서 거칠게 말하는 모습에 쓰고, 욕설이 없어도 상대를 무시하는 말투면 막말이라고 해요. '험담'은 없는 데서 흉보는 것이라 달라요. 뉴스에서는 '막말 논란'처럼 명사로도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It describes talking harshly out of anger; even without swear words, a dismissive tone counts as 막말. '험담' is speaking ill of someone behind their back, which is different. In news the noun appears often, as in '막말 논란'.

examples.ko: 어부가 새벽에 배를 타고 바다로 나갔어요.
examples.en: The fisherman went out to sea by boat at dawn.
My grandfather worked as a fisherman when he was young.
The fishermen are tidying up their nets.

examples.ko: 그 섬 마을 사람들은 대부분 어부예요.
examples.en: Most people in that island village are fishermen.
I bought fresh fish directly from a fisherman.

examples.ko: 태풍 소식에 어부의 가족들이 걱정이 많아요.
examples.en: With the typhoon news, the fishermen's families are very worried.

explain: 고기 잡는 일을 직업으로 하는 사람이에요. 낚시를 취미로 하는 사람은 '낚시꾼'이라고 해서 구분해요. 요즘은 '어민'이라는 말도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means a person who fishes for a living. Someone who fishes as a hobby is a 낚시꾼, so the two are distinguished. Nowadays 어민 is also widely used.
